question: To which of the following dynasties were the Vatapi Chalukyas tributary princes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kadambas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Vatapi Chalukyas were initially under the Kadamba dynasty, which makes the correct answer option 4.
 
• This relationship signifies the complex feudal system of ancient and medieval India, where smaller kingdoms often paid tribute to larger empires.
 
• The Kadambas were a South Indian dynasty that ruled much of modern-day Karnataka. They were known for their contributions to temple architecture and support of Jainism and Hinduism.
 
• The Chalukyas of Vatapi later emerged as a significant power, establishing a vast empire that influenced South Indian politics and culture.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 1) Kalyani Chalukyas
 The Kalyani Chalukyas were successors to the Vatapi Chalukyas, ruling parts of southern and central India between the 10th and 12th centuries.
 
 

 2) Cholas
 The Cholas were a prominent dynasty in southern India and at times were rivals of the Chalukyas, known for their naval power and monumental architecture.
 
 

 3) Pallavas
 The Pallavas, ruling parts of southern India, were contemporaries and often adversaries of the Chalukyas, known for their rock-cut architecture and patronage of art.
